description: Insecure MQTT Communication Without enforced TLS encryption, MQTT traffic between IoT devices and AWS IoT Core travels in plaintext or with weak encryption. Attackers within network range or with access to network infrastructure could intercept this traffic. An attacker could set up a network sniffer near IoT devices or compromise network equipment to capture MQTT messages, potentially exposing sensitive device data and credentials. They could also inject false data to trigger unnecessary maintenance alerts.
references: recommendation: Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for all MQTT connections using AWS IoT Core's built-in security features
recommendation: Implement device authentication and authorization

description: Excessive Costs from False Positives The system processes IoT sensor data through multiple stages (Kinesis, Lambda, SageMaker) to predict maintenance needs. False positives could trigger unnecessary processing, storage, and alerts, consuming resources and increasing costs. An attacker could manipulate sensor data or exploit model vulnerabilities to trigger false predictions, causing system overload and excessive AWS resource consumption.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Implement rate limiting and anomaly detection
recommendation: Enhance data validation and model monitoring

description: Insufficient IAM Role Segmentation Several IAM roles in the CDK code use broad permissions (e.g., AmazonSageMakerFullAccess) or have resource wildcards (*) in their policies. This violates the principle of least privilege. If an attacker compromises a service using these roles, they could potentially access unrelated resources or escalate privileges due to overly permissive policies.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material

description: Insufficient Edge Device Security Greengrass core devices run ML models at the edge and have significant permissions to interact with AWS services. Physical access or remote exploitation could allow attackers to manipulate the device or extract sensitive data. An attacker with physical access could tamper with the Greengrass core device to extract ML models, modify inference results, or use the device's credentials to access AWS services.
references: recommendation: Implement edge device security controls
recommendation: Enhance edge monitoring and compliance

description: Time Series Data Exposure Time series data in Timestream contains detailed operational metrics that could reveal sensitive information about device operations and maintenance patterns. Unauthorized access could expose business intelligence or enable targeted attacks. An attacker gaining access to QuickSight dashboards or exploiting overly permissive Timestream policies could extract historical data to analyze patterns and plan targeted attacks on maintenance windows.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
